finding: Held: this file is not ready to publish. There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so there is nothing to call too wide or too narrow; this is a first build. What can be built (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2012 Toyota Corolla about $206-$740 (parts $146.26-$595.67, 0.5-0.9 hour); midsize 2015 Subaru Forester 2.5i about $309-$583 (parts $236.95-$439.45, 0.6-0.9 hour); truck 2015 Ram 1500 5.7L about $616-$1,152 (parts $508-$832, 0.9-2 hours). For the luxury 2012 Lexus ES 350 only the top can be built, up to about $821 for one of its two rear mufflers (genuine $676.97, 0.5-0.9 hour), because no aftermarket price passed the sourcing test. The part is most of every total: the labor is roughly $60 to $320. The truck's low end is too high. Its low parts price is a premium stainless performance-brand direct-fit muffler ($508), the only direct-fit part found on a page that says new and lists the 2015 truck. A stock-style Walker muffler listed new for the same truck is $148.26, but it is sold without pipes and has to be cut in and clamped or welded, which is a different job from this unit, so it is kept as a cross-check only; a driver quoted well under $616 for a welded-in muffler on this truck is probably being quoted that job. What is null and why: the low parts price for the luxury example. Walker direct-fit mufflers are sold for it and prices of roughly $129-$211 were seen, but each page failed one test: it printed no model years, did not say the part was new, or showed no price. How solid the labor times are: two examples have a time for the example vehicle, and neither is a maker document. The Forester's 0.6 hour is a Subaru book time quoted by a named mechanic, and the Ram's 2 hours is a parts seller's figure written for an owner fitting a bolt-on muffler at home (two listings for the truck say 2 hours and one says 1 hour). Every other range end is a maker-stated time for a different vehicle: Hyundai's 0.5 hour for the centre muffler on the 2014-2015 Tucson and FCA's 0.9 hour for the muffler on the 2015 Ram 2500 and 3500 5.7L. No maker-stated time with a unit was found for the Corolla, Forester, Ram 1500 or ES 350. Four maker figures support the range without being used as ends because each includes an inspection or prints no unit: Mazda 0.4 hour (2019 CX-5 Turbo), FCA 0.3 hour (2020 Jeep Cherokee, inspect and replace), Kia 0.4 hour (2023 Sportage centre muffler, inspect and replace) and Subaru 0.2 with no unit (2015-2017 Legacy and Outback). These suggest warranty times are often shorter than 0.5 hour, so the labor range here is not low. All of them are times for bolted joints that come apart; a rusted flange or seized bolts on an older car add time, and the 0.9 hour top does not allow for that. On some vehicles the larger main muffler is part of a centre pipe that costs far more from the maker and is outside this unit; a quote for 'a muffler' on such a vehicle may be for that part. Benchmarks, from three publishers with a full installed price: RepairPal's national average is $1,138-$1,190 with parts at about $1,035, far above the built totals, while its Corolla figure ($625-$661) sits inside the built economy range and its Silverado and F-150 figures ($706-$830) sit inside the built truck range. The national figure appears to price a dearer genuine part or a larger exhaust section; the page does not say which, so that is a reading, not a finding. CostHelper gives $75-$750 or more (its readers report $80-$647, average $280, in reports dated 2010 to 2020) and Synchrony's article gives $175-$450 or more, with a maker's original muffler at up to $1,000. Both are lower than RepairPal and overlap the built economy and midsize ranges; their low ends are for cheaper universal or welded-in mufflers than the direct-fit parts priced here. A fourth entry is parts only. Confidence is low because one low parts price is missing, the truck low is a premium part, half the labor range ends are not for the example vehicle and no example has a maker-stated time. This is an estimate, not a quote and not a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds new gaskets, clamps, bolts and rubber hangers, and labor to cut or heat rusted fasteners. Many shops recommend replacing the connecting pipe or resonator at the same time, and on cars with two rear mufflers the second one. If no bolt-on part is used, a muffler shop may cut the old one out and weld in a universal muffler, which is priced differently from this estimate. Also possible: a diagnosis or exhaust leak check fee, shop supplies and sales tax. A muffler replaced under a recall, service campaign or warranty extension is done by the dealer at no charge, so check for open campaigns first. An exhaust leak ahead of the muffler can let fumes into the cabin and should be looked at promptly.
